sections.title: Jews in the Medieval and Early Modern Worlds
sections.description: This course covers the long period of Jewish history from the fall of the Roman Empire and the rise of Islam until the French and American Revolutions. In this period Jewish life shifted from its Mediterranean origins to new European settlements and patterns of living, with important consequences for relations between Christians, Muslims, and Jews right up until the present. This was an era of mass migrations, mass religious movements, and mass media. Our course will cover violent encounters like expulsions, crusades, and blood libels alongside daily contacts and creative exchanges between Jews and their neighbors in the realms of science, medicine, law, and mysticism. By exploring the experiences of Jews across the Middle East, Europe, and the Atlantic world, we will examine the ways in which a minority group—thought of as distinct and deviant—has both its own stories to tell and offers alternative ways to think about world civilizations.
